title: When Is Self-Hosting AI Actually Cheaper?

images.alt: A balance scale weighs a local GPU server against a blue cloud and usage tokens, illustrating the tradeoff between ownership and pay-per-use costs.
images.caption: A lower cost per token only helps if the workload can carry the cost of owning and operating the server.

images.alt: Illustrative assumptions: $3,600 machine over 36 months; 730 powered-on hours monthly; 100 W idle and 350 W active; electricity $0.30/kWh; 2 extra operations hours at $75/hour; $20 other monthly costs; 1 accepted request/second.
images.caption: Illustrative local-host assumptions. Illustrative assumptions; no measured hardware performance or vendor prices.

images.alt: Illustrative monthly local versus API costs: 10,000 requests, $292.11 versus $30; 100,000, $293.98 versus $300; 500,000, $302.32 versus $1,500.
images.caption: Monthly accepted requests: 10,000, 100,000 and 500,000. Costs use illustrative assumptions; extra local maintenance can reverse a narrow saving.

images.alt: At 0.2, 1 and 3 assumed requests/second, break-even volumes are 100,800, 97,980 and 97,526 requests/month. Serving 100,000 requests needs 138.89, 27.78 and 9.26 active hours respectively.
images.caption: Rows assume 0.2, 1 and 3 accepted requests/second. These are capacity scenarios, not measured hardware results.

seo_title: Self-Hosting AI vs API: Costs and Break-Even
seo_description: Compare self-hosted AI with API costs using a transparent monthly model: GPU ownership, maintenance, utilization, latency, and the break-even workload.

title: Your Kafka Consumers Are Becoming a Workflow Engine

images.alt: Video job cards move through a branching mechanical workflow; an orange gate stops one branch while another continues toward completion.
images.caption: Once a job can branch, wait and be cancelled, its state needs an owner beyond the next message.

images.alt: Six failure cases and decisions: deduplicate requests; reconcile timed-out dispatch; record late completion without notification; match old results to operation identity; persist expired deadlines; recover expired leases while preserving step identity.
images.caption: Failure decisions for the hypothetical video-export workflow. The cancellation contract determines which transitions remain allowed.

seo_title: Kafka Workflows: Cancellation, Retries and State
seo_description: When Kafka consumers coordinate long-running jobs, retries are only the start. Explore cancellation, idempotency, durable state, and workflow ownership.
